title: Climate and disaster alerts
metaTitle: Climate and disaster alerts for Bangladesh
subtitle: How temperature and rainfall in each division compared with the long-term average over the last 12 months, and cyclone, flood and drought alerts for Bangladesh.

anomalies.title: The last 12 months compared with normal
anomalies.period: {from} to {to} · NASA POWER estimates for each division headquarters (satellite and model data, not weather-station readings).
anomalies.whatBody: Each month is compared with the long-term average for the same calendar month — the “normal”. This difference is called an anomaly. A temperature of +0.5 °C means the month was half a degree warmer than usual. Rainfall is shown as a percentage of normal: 100% is a typical month, 50% is half the usual rain and 150% is one and a half times as much.
anomalies.dryNote: From November to March normal rainfall is only a few millimetres, so the percentage can swing a lot. Check the millimetres in the table as well.
anomalies.baseline: Normal = NASA POWER monthly average for {start}–{end}.
anomalies.baselineUnknown: Normal = NASA POWER long-term monthly average.
anomalies.scaleNote: Every chart uses the same scale: up to ±{max} °C for temperature and 0–200% of normal for rainfall (taller bars are cut off at 200%).
anomalies.chartTemp: {division}: monthly temperature difference from normal, {from} to {to}. Average {value} °C.
anomalies.chartRain: {division}: monthly rainfall as a percentage of normal, {from} to {to}. Total {value}% of normal.
anomalies.tableTemp: Monthly mean temperature in °C (difference from normal in brackets)
anomalies.tableRain: Monthly rainfall in mm (percentage of normal in brackets)
anomalies.unavailable: Climate data from NASA POWER is temporarily unavailable. Please try again later.
anomalies.missingDivisions: Data for these divisions could not be loaded: {names}.

alerts.title: Disaster alerts
alerts.historyTitle: GDACS alerts for Bangladesh in the last 12 months
alerts.intro: GDACS, the Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System of the United Nations and the European Commission, issues automatic alerts for cyclones, floods and droughts worldwide. These are not official national warnings — follow the Bangladesh Meteorological Department and the Department of Disaster Management.
alerts.none: No active GDACS alerts for Bangladesh
alerts.noneInYear: GDACS recorded no cyclone, flood or drought events for Bangladesh in the last 12 months.
alerts.activeNote: “Active” means the event is ongoing or ended within the last 7 days.
alerts.levelHelp: The alert level is GDACS’s estimate of the likely impact on people: red high, orange medium, green low.
alerts.reportLabel: GDACS report: {name} (opens in a new tab)
alerts.unavailable: GDACS alerts are temporarily unavailable. Please try again in a few minutes.
